content.text: I fixed all five defects with targeted find/replace patches across four files.

input.summary: All five verified findings are repaired by exact patches: the undisclosed indicator-housing port geometry is removed from FIG-6 (and its echo in FIG-2), FIG-3 now states the open communication between the inter-cassette space and the upper ends of both guide ducts that the disclosed flow sequence requires, FIG-1 states the inverted lid attitude once and expresses the gasket, rib and axis relationships as closed-condition relationships, the Detailed Description no longer asserts an undisclosed condensation mechanism on cooled duct surfaces, and claim 16 now uses the disclosure's "remains accessible" relationship for the pull tab instead of "thereby exposing". Two consequential edits inside FIG-6 (the stem bullet and the closing statement) were patched in the same answer so no reference to the deleted housing interior remains. No claim scope, numeral, embodiment or disclosed subject matter was changed, and the numeral table needed no change since every affected numeral keeps the same part and the same figure assignments. Note, as the brief requires: no prior-art search was run, so the art on hand may be incomplete.
changes: figures/FIG-6.md: replaced the 'Mechanical exposure indicator 80' bullet, deleting the undisclosed housing port geometry (open toward the bore, open at its outer side, interior aligned with the bore, stem's outer end lying within the housing and short of that outer side); the assembly is now a schematic unnumbered plain outline shown in the retained condition.

figures/FIG-6.md: amended the 'Indicator stem 82' bullet and the closing statement so neither refers to the interior of the deleted housing, while keeping the bore, the thermal coupling to cassette 44 and the omitted intervening structure unchanged.

figures/FIG-2.md: changed the 'Shell side wall 14' bullet so the left-wall feature is the schematically shown mechanical exposure indicator with a bore through that wall, not a small housing standing proud of the wall.

figures/FIG-3.md: amended the 'Downward guide duct 48' bullet to state each duct is open at its upper end to the blank open space above and between the cassettes 44, resolving the geometry that previously left no path.
figures/FIG-3.md: amended the closing statement to say the inter-cassette space is open at its upper part to the upper end of each duct, so the disclosed flow sequence is drawable as described.

figures/FIG-1.md: rewrote the 'Insulated lid 60' bullet so the inverted attitude is stated once and the gasket 64 is described as in register with the upper edge 16, which it meets when the lid is closed.
figures/FIG-1.md: rewrote the 'Depending indexing rib 62' bullet so rib engagement is expressed as a closed-condition relationship.

figures/FIG-1.md: in the 'Removable thermal module 40' bullet, replaced 'directly below the depending indexing rib 62' with a closed-condition statement that the recess receives the rib when the lid is closed.
figures/FIG-1.md: amended the alignment statement so the inverted lid 60 is drawn above the module 40 on the same upright axis, rather than lying above it as an upright body would.

draft/08-detailed-description.md: replaced the condensate sentence so it states only that condensate collecting within the guide ducts runs down and leaves through the condensate discharge openings 56 into the shallow condensate channel 70, removing the undisclosed 'condenses on the cooled surfaces' mechanism.

draft/09-claims.md: rewrote the third step of claim 16 so the pull tab remains accessible when the removable product tray is removed, matching the disclosure and the Detailed Description, with the channel receiving condensate from the lower-end discharge openings.

patches.find: - Mechanical exposure indicator 80: the indicator assembly at the outer surface of the shell side wall 14, comprising the stem 82, the latch 84, the spring 86 and an unnumbered housing that stands proud of that outer surface, the numeral 80 being led to the assembly as a whole; the housing is shown schematically as a hatched box of modest size, open toward the bore and open at its outer side, its interior blank and aligned with the bore, the outer end of the stem 82 lying within the housing and short of that outer side in the retained condition shown, so that the stem 82 becomes visible from outside the carrier when the spring 86 has moved it to the latched exposed position.
patches.replace: - Mechanical exposure indicator 80: the indicator assembly at the outer surface of the shell side wall 14, comprising the stem 82, the latch 84 and the spring 86, the assembly shown schematically within an unnumbered plain outline and the numeral 80 being led to the assembly as a whole; the indicator 80 is shown in the retained condition, the stem 82 not yet having been moved by the spring 86 to the latched exposed position in which it is visible from outside the carrier.
patches.why: Removes the undisclosed housing port geometry (outer-side opening, interior aligned with the bore, axial depth of the stem's outer end), which the disclosure never states and which is substantive functional-surface geometry even in a schematic view.

patches.find: - Indicator stem 82: an elongate bar lying in the bore and in the interior of the housing, drawn with its own outline and its own hatching pattern distinct from that of the shell side wall 14.
patches.replace: - Indicator stem 82: an elongate bar lying in the bore, drawn with its own outline and its own hatching pattern distinct from that of the shell side wall 14.
patches.why: The housing interior no longer exists in the brief; this keeps the stem bullet consistent without adding any position or depth relationship.

patches.find: - The stem 82 extends from the interior of the housing of the indicator 80 through the thickness of the shell side wall 14, its inner end lying at the inner side of the shell side wall 14 and being thermally coupled to the cassette 44 shown at the right of the view, the intervening structure being omitted.
patches.replace: - The stem 82 extends from the indicator 80 at the outer surface of the shell side wall 14 through the thickness of that wall, its inner end lying at the inner side of the shell side wall 14 and being thermally coupled to the cassette 44 shown at the right of the view, the intervening structure being omitted.
patches.why: Same consequential fix: the closing statement must not refer to the deleted housing interior, while the disclosed thermal coupling is preserved verbatim.

patches.find: A small housing, shown schematically, stands proud of the outer face of the left shell side wall 14 at the level of the module 40, with a bore through that wall.
patches.replace: The mechanical exposure indicator is shown schematically at the outer face of the left shell side wall 14 at the level of the module 40, with a bore through that wall.
patches.why: Removes the echo of the undisclosed housing from FIG-2 so the two briefs stay synchronized on the indicator region.

patches.find: - Downward guide duct 48: two blank open upright passages, one on each side, each between the outboard surface of one cassette 44 and the nearer outboard web of the frame 42, each open at its lower end at the bottom of the view.
patches.replace: - Downward guide duct 48: two blank open upright passages, one on each side, each between the outboard surface of one cassette 44 and the nearer outboard web of the frame 42, each open at its upper end to the blank open space above and between the cassettes 44 and open at its lower end at the bottom of the view.
patches.why: Supplies the open communication that the disclosed flow sequence requires, resolving the internal inconsistency without adding cassette proportion, contact, or new function.

patches.find: - The space between the two cassettes 44 is continuous with the opening 46 below it and communicates with both ducts 48, so that air entering the opening 46 passes along the opposed faces of the cassettes 44 and into the ducts 48.
patches.replace: - The space between the two cassettes 44 is continuous with the opening 46 below it and is open at its upper part to the upper end of each duct 48, so that air entering the opening 46 passes along the opposed faces of the cassettes 44 and into the ducts 48.
patches.why: States the communication in terms the described elements actually provide, so the renderer has consistent geometry for the disclosed path.

patches.find: - Insulated lid 60: a rectangular slab, shown schematically, floating above the module 40, matching the shell 10 in plan, shown turned over about its front edge in the same perspective so that its underside faces the viewer. A compressible lid gasket 64 is drawn on that underside, shown schematically as a continuous band running around it and positioned to face the upper edge 16.
patches.replace: - Insulated lid 60: a rectangular slab, shown schematically, floating above the module 40, matching the shell 10 in plan, shown inverted in the same perspective so that its underside faces the viewer. A compressible lid gasket 64 is drawn on that underside, shown schematically as a continuous band running around it in register with the upper edge 16, which it meets when the lid 60 is closed.
patches.why: States the inverted attitude once and expresses the gasket relationship as a closed-condition relationship that an inverted body can satisfy.

patches.find: - Depending indexing rib 62: a short straight rib projecting from the underside of the lid 60, that underside facing the viewer in this view, shown schematically.
patches.replace: - Depending indexing rib 62: a short straight rib projecting from the underside of the lid 60, that underside facing the viewer in this view, shown schematically, the rib 62 entering the recess in the upper surface of the module 40 when the lid 60 is closed.
patches.why: Removes the contradiction between a viewer-facing rib and a rib lying directly above the module recess in the exploded view.

patches.find: an unnumbered upwardly open recess being formed in its upper surface directly below the depending indexing rib 62;
patches.replace: an unnumbered upwardly open recess being formed in its upper surface positioned to receive the depending indexing rib 62 when the lid 60 is closed;
patches.why: The recess cannot lie directly below a rib that projects toward the viewer; the closed-condition wording is consistent with the depiction and with the disclosed registration.

patches.find: - The tray 20 and the module 40 are aligned over the opening of the shell 10 so that they would descend into it, and the lid 60 lies above the module 40 on the same upright axis.
patches.replace: - The tray 20 and the module 40 are aligned over the opening of the shell 10 so that they would descend into it, and the inverted lid 60 is drawn above the module 40 on the same upright axis.
patches.why: An inverted body cannot be described as poised to descend in its use attitude; this states only where it is drawn.

patches.find: Moisture that condenses on the cooled surfaces within the downward guide ducts 48 runs down the ducts and leaves them through the condensate discharge openings 56, rather than collecting on the payload or standing in the bottom of the interior.
patches.replace: Condensate that collects within the downward guide ducts 48 runs down the ducts and leaves them through the condensate discharge openings 56 into the shallow condensate channel 70, rather than standing in the bottom of the interior.
patches.why: Removes the undisclosed operating mechanism (condensation on cooled duct surfaces) while keeping the disclosed discharge of condensate from the lower ends of the ducts into the channel.

patches.find: lifting a removable product tray out of the insulated outer shell, thereby exposing a pull tab of a removable absorbent wick lying in a shallow condensate channel that extends around the removable product tray and that receives condensate from condensate discharge openings at lower ends of the downward guide ducts;
patches.replace: lifting a removable product tray out of the insulated outer shell, a pull tab of a removable absorbent wick lying in a shallow condensate channel that extends around the removable product tray remaining accessible when the removable product tray is removed, the shallow condensate channel receiving condensate from condensate discharge openings at lower ends of the downward guide ducts;
patches.why: Aligns claim 16 with the disclosure and the Detailed Description, which state the pull tab remains accessible when the tray is removed rather than being exposed by removal.
